title: [YouPass Collect] - The percentage of the Australian workforce in five industries
prompt: The graph below shows the percentage of the Australian workforce in five industries between 1962 and 2012. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the proportion of workers employed in five different sectors of the Australian economy over a 50-year period from 1962 to 2012.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while the service sector witnessed a substantial upward trend throughout the period shown, manufacturing experienced a significant decline. Additionally, services consistently remained the highest-employing sector, while the remaining three industries maintained relatively stable but low percentages of the total workforce.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the two dominant sectors, in 1962, the service sector employed approximately 53% of the workforce, which was about twice the figure for manufacturing, at 27%. Subsequently, the service sector then experienced a steady increase over the following decades, reaching around 78% by 2012. In contrast, manufacturing showed a continuous downward trend, particularly sharp between 1972 and 1992, before settling at roughly 11% in the final year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the other three industries, in 1962, the agricultural sector accounted for 12% of Australia's workforce, compared to 10% employed in the construction industry. Thereafter, while agricultural employment declined slightly to about 4% by 2012, the construction sector remained relatively stable, ending the period at approximately 10%. Mining consistently accounted for the smallest share of employment, showing minimal variation between 1% and 2% throughout the entire period.
